questions: Are the repeated leg movements the main reason you are being evaluated today?
Do you feel an irresistible urge to move your legs before these movements occur?
Do the movements provide temporary relief of an uncomfortable sensation in your legs?
Do these symptoms occur mainly when you are sitting or lying still?
Are they worse in the evening or at night?
Do they interfere with falling asleep or staying asleep?
Are the movements involuntary, rather than something you deliberately do?
Have these symptoms been present for more than three months?
Have they recently become more frequent or severe?
Do you have pain in either knee or leg?
Is one leg significantly more swollen, red, or warm than the other?
Have you developed new weakness, numbness, or tingling in either leg?
Do you have low-back pain that travels down either leg?
Have you had any recent fall, injury, surgery, prolonged travel, or period of bed rest?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed the dose of any medication?
Do you use caffeine, nicotine, alcohol, or stimulant medications regularly?
Has anyone observed your legs making repeated movements while you sleep?
Have you ever been diagnosed with anemia, kidney disease, thyroid disease, Parkinson’s disease, or another neurologic condition?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional movement disorder with distractible involuntary leg movements, occurring in the setting of overt thyrotoxicosis

ALTERNATIVE: Thyrotoxic chorea

ALTERNATIVE: Functional tremor or myoclonus related to anxiety or stimulant use

ALTERNATIVE: Early autoimmune hyperthyroidism, most likely Graves disease, causing secondary hyperkinetic movements
